title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 88 sits in a section on 'Correspondances entre dispositions et entre synthèses'. Before it, Grothendieck works with orthogonality-type structures: sets carrying a symmetric relation |∘| ('disjoint'), which he calls 'disjoncteurs' or 'dispositions'. Their saturated subsets form the poset Σ_E. As a warm-up analogy he takes two plain sets E, E', viewed as trivial dispositions where |∘| is ordinary disjointness of subsets.

(1) A relation R ⊂ E×E' is the same thing as a map α: E → P(E'), x ↦ R(x).

(2) This map extends to the direct-image map α_* = ᾱ: P(E) → P(E'), A ↦ ⋃_{x∈A} α(x). This map preserves arbitrary sups (unions), including the empty one. Conversely, every arbitrary-sup-preserving map φ: P(E) → P(E') has this form for a unique α, namely α(x) = φ({x}), because A = Sup_{x∈A}{x}. In modern terms, P(E) is the free complete join-semilattice on E. Hence relations E → E' correspond to sup-lattice morphisms P(E) → P(E'), i.e. Rel ≃ the Kleisli category of the powerset monad, sitting inside the category of sup-lattices.

(3) Let β: E' → P(E) be the transposed relation R^t. The key identity (*) is:
  ∀A ⊂ E, A' ⊂ E': α_*(A) ∩ A' = ∅ ⟺ A ∩ β_*(A') = ∅.
His proof unfolds the left side: for all x' ∈ A', no x ∈ A has (x,x') ∈ R. Equivalently, every pair (x,x') ∈ A×A' lies in the complement relation R̄. That condition is symmetric, which gives the right side; the conclusion is completed on the next page.

Equivalently, α_* is left adjoint to A' ↦ ∁β_*(∁A'), the 'box' operator. In Jónsson–Tarski language, α_* and β_* are conjugate operators.

Purpose: on the next page (Prop. 3) the identity is promoted to a definition. For general disjoncteurs (E,|∘|), (E',|∘|), a pair α: E → P(E'), β: E' → P(E) is called 'transposed' if x |∘| β(x') ⟺ α(x) |∘| x'. Such a pair induces maps α_*, β_* between the lattices of saturated sets Σ_E ⇄ Σ_{E'}, obtained by taking the saturation supp° of the image. These maps satisfy the same orthogonality-adjunction and are compatible with saturation. In effect this builds a category of orthogonality spaces whose morphisms are 'adjointable' relations.
errors: No mathematical error. 'Commute aux Sup quelconques' must include the empty sup (φ(∅)=∅) for the converse to hold; the word 'quelconques' covers this.

Small notational overload: ᾱ is used for the extension α_*, while R̄ denotes the complement relation. On the next page the bar is also used for set complements/closures, which may confuse readers but does not affect the logic.

ideas.what: Relations E→E' correspond bijectively to arbitrary-union-preserving maps P(E)→P(E'), via α ↦ α_* and φ ↦ (x ↦ φ({x})).
ideas.modern_name: P(E) as the free sup-lattice; Rel ≃ Kleisli category of the powerset monad, embedded in SupLat
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (lattice theory; Joyal–Tierney 1984 for the sup-lattice viewpoint)

ideas.what: Disjointness identity α_*(A) ∩ A' = ∅ ⟺ A ∩ (R^t)_*(A') = ∅ for a relation and its transpose.
ideas.modern_name: Conjugate operators (Jónsson–Tarski); diamond/box adjunction of tense/modal logic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jónsson–Tarski 1951 (Boolean algebras with operators); Prior's tense logic

ideas.what: Using this identity to define 'transposed' pairs of correspondences between sets with a symmetric orthogonality relation, inducing maps between the lattices of orthogonally closed sets (developed on the following page).
ideas.modern_name: Adjointable maps / morphisms of orthogonality spaces; Foulis-style adjoint pairs between orthocomplemented lattices; Galois connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis (Baer *-semigroups, 1960s); Dacey/Foulis–Randall orthogonality spaces; Paseka–Vetterlein, categories of orthogonality spaces (c. 2020–22); Heunen–Jacobs dagger-kernel categories (2010)

missed.claim: In unpublished 1986 notes, Grothendieck sets up 'transposed' correspondences between orthogonality structures ('disjoncteurs'), defined by α(x) |∘| x' ⟺ x |∘| β(x'), as the morphisms between such structures. This is essentially the adjointability notion recently used for categories of orthogonality spaces (Paseka–Vetterlein) and in quantum-logic/dagger-category work. He motivates it via the Jónsson–Tarski conjugacy of a relation and its transpose. No link between this Grothendieck material and that literature appears to be recorded.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck independently arriving at the categorical framework for orthogonality spaces and closure lattices that is currently being developed in quantum-logic and dagger-category research. On this page itself the content is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is elementary: relations as sup-lattice maps, plus the conjugacy identity for a relation and its transpose. Its interest lies only in setting up the 'transposed correspondence' notion for orthogonality spaces on the next page, which parallels later work but is classical in spirit (Foulis, Jónsson–Tarski).
transcription_corrections: Line 2 '[?]-application' is likely just 'application' (possibly 'Sup-application'); the image shows a short word before 'application'.
In (*) the right-hand side should read 'A |∘| β_*(A')' (the symbol is partially written as '|'), matching the left-hand side 'α_*(A) |∘| A''.
The last line reads '∀x ∈ A, x' ∈ A' on a (x,x') ∉ R i.e. (x,x') ∈ R̄' (R̄ = complement of R), as transcribed; the earlier line has '∄ x ∈ A avec x' ∈ α(x)'.

The margin note likely reads roughly: 'J'écris ᾱ ou α_* pour l'application de P(E) dans P(E') des ensembles de parties de E, E', en considérant α comme une application...' plus a second note about 'compatibilité ... α_*', both largely illegible.
The page number in the header shows a stamp ('85'?), while the archive foliation is 88.
